from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Sherlock Bones, our probabilistic detective dog.",
            "He hears a rustle in the bushes nearby.",
            "Sherlock believes there's a 10% chance it's a cat.",
            "If it's a cat, his ears twitch 90% often.",
            "His ears just twitched! Is it really a cat?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PRIOR = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOG = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_CAT = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_WIND = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet Sherlock Bones (Dog Icon)
        head = Circle(radius=0.5, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1)
        left_ear = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1).rotate(PI/6)
        right_ear = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/6)
        left_ear.shift(LEFT*0.35 + UP*0.4)
        right_ear.shift(RIGHT*0.35 + UP*0.4)
        
        eyes = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLACK).shift(LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.1),
            Dot(color=BLACK).shift(RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        )
        nose = Triangle(color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.08).rotate(PI).shift(DOWN*0.1)
        
        dog = VGroup(head, left_ear, right_ear, eyes, nose)
        self.place_at_grid(dog, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DOG))
        self.play(FadeIn(dog))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rustle in the bushes (visualized as a shaking bush)
        bush = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN_E, fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT*0.2*i)
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(bush, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(bush))
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(LEFT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(LEFT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sherlock believes 10% Cat / 90% Wind (Thought Bubble)
        bubble_outline = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.3, height=1.5, width=2.5, color=WHITE)
        cat_text = Text("Cat (10%)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        wind_text = Text("Wind (90%)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        thought_content = VGroup(cat_text, wind_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        thought_bubble = VGroup(bubble_outline, thought_content)
        self.place_at_grid(thought_bubble, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        connector_dots = VGroup(
            Dot(radius=0.05, color=WHITE),
            Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE),
            Dot(radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        connector_dots.move_to(self.grid["C4"])

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PRIOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(connector_dots), FadeIn(thought_bubble))
        # Highlight Cat as Prior
        self.play(cat_text.animate.set_color(COLOR_PRIOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # If it's a cat, his ears twitch 90% often
        twitch_prob = Text("P(Twitch | Cat) = 90%", font_size=16, color=COLOR_CAT)
        self.place_at_grid(twitch_prob, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_CAT))
        self.play(FadeIn(twitch_prob))
        
        # Twitching animation
        self.play(
            left_ear.animate.rotate(PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            right_ear.animate.rotate(-PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            run_time=0.2
        )
        self.play(
            left_ear.animate.rotate(-PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            right_ear.animate.rotate(PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            run_time=0.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # His ears just twitched! Is it really a cat?
        question = Text("P(Cat | Twitch)?", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(question, "F4", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Final twitch
        self.play(
            left_ear.animate.rotate(PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            right_ear.animate.rotate(-PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            run_time=0.1
        )
        self.play(
            left_ear.animate.rotate(-PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            right_ear.animate.rotate(PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            run_time=0.1
        )
        self.play(Write(question))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite: Conditional Probability & The Shrinking Universe"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Conditional probability looks at a specific subset of outcomes.",
            "If event B occurs, our entire universe shrinks.",
            "We only care about A where it overlaps B."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors for elements
        color_a = BLUE_D
        color_b = GREEN_D
        color_overlap = YELLOW
        color_universe = GRAY_E

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Step 1: Show Venn Diagram with circles A and B.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_a)
        
        # Universe Rectangle (using area B2 to E6 to keep Col 1 empty)
        universe = Rectangle(width=5, height=4, color=color_universe, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(universe, 'B2', 'E6')
        universe_label = Text("Universe (Ω)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(universe_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Circles A and B
        circle_a = Circle(radius=1.2, color=color_a, fill_opacity=0.3)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=1.2, color=color_b, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # Positioning them to overlap
        self.place_at_grid(circle_a, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(circle_b, 'C5')
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=color_a)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=color_b)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        venn_group = VGroup(circle_a, circle_b, label_a, label_b)

        self.play(
            Create(universe),
            FadeIn(universe_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(circle_a),
            FadeIn(circle_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Step 2: Fade out everything except circle B and A \cap B.
        # "Shrink the universe"
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_b)
        
        # Create a highlight version of Circle B as the new universe
        circle_b_highlight = circle_b.copy().set_stroke(width=6, color=color_overlap)
        
        self.play(
            universe.animate.set_opacity(0.05),
            universe_label.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            circle_a.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2).set_fill(opacity=0.1),
            label_a.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            Create(circle_b_highlight),
            circle_b.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Step 3: Show formula P(A|B) = P(A \cap B) / P(B) next to Venn.
        # Highlight A \cap B clearly.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_overlap)
        
        # Intersection highlight
        intersection = Intersection(circle_a, circle_b, color=color_overlap, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        # Formula - using place_in_area for multi-column spanning (B002)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}",
            font_size=36,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Highlight the formula parts
        formula[0][2:5].set_color(color_overlap) # A|B
        formula[0][7:11].set_color(color_overlap) # A \cap B
        formula[0][13:14].set_color(color_b) # B
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'E2', 'F6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(intersection),
            Write(formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines from storyboard
        # Title: "Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone"
        # 1. Independence means event B provides no new information.
        # 2. Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A.
        # 3. The proportion of A remains constant across the universe.
        
        self.setup_layout("Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone", [
            "Independence means event B provides no new information.",
            "Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A.",
            "The proportion of A remains constant across the universe."
        ])
        
        # Colors - Hex format as requested
        COLOR_A = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_B = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_INTERSECT = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Independence means event B provides no new information."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Universe Square
        # Area B3 to E5 (Rows B-E, Cols 3-5). 
        # Width: Col 3, 4, 5. Height: Row B, C, D, E.
        universe = Square(side_length=3.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(universe, "B3", "E5")
        
        u_label = Text("Universe", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(u_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Two independent circles A and B
        circle_a = Circle(radius=0.8, color=COLOR_A, fill_opacity=0.2)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=0.8, color=COLOR_B, fill_opacity=0.2)
        
        # Centers within the square
        self.place_at_grid(circle_a, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(circle_b, "D4") # Vertical overlap
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_A)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_B)
        
        # External labels to avoid bounding box overlap (B001)
        # Using Col 2 and Col 6 which are outside the B3-E5 universe box.
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(universe), FadeIn(u_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(circle_a, label_a), FadeIn(circle_b, label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Highlight knowing B (the condition)
        self.play(circle_b.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.5))
        
        # Highlight intersection A in B
        # Use Intersection mobject (Community Edition v0.19.0)
        intersect = Intersection(circle_a, circle_b, color=COLOR_INTERSECT, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(intersect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The proportion of A remains constant across the universe."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERSECT))
        
        # Proportion text at top (Area A4 to A6)
        ratio_text = MathTex(
            "\\frac{P(A \\cap B)}{P(B)} = P(A)",
            font_size=32, color=COLOR_INTERSECT
        )
        self.place_in_area(ratio_text, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Definitive equality at bottom (Area F3 to F6)
        formula = MathTex("P(A|B) = P(A)", color=COLOR_INTERSECT)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "F3", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio_text))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.",
            "Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.",
            "Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.",
            "Divide by the total probability of that evidence.",
            "Now you have the updated posterior probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors defined in requirements
        PRIOR_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        LIKELIHOOD_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        EVIDENCE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        POSTERIOR_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = WHITE
        DIM_COLOR = GRAY

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.
        # Write the full Bayes formula P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
        
        # Formula parts: 0:P(A|B), 1:=, 2:{, 3:P(B|A), 4:P(A), 5:\over, 6:P(B), 7:}
        # Using string splitting to allow individual coloring
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{", "P(B|A)", "P(A)", "\\over", "P(B)", "}"
        )
        
        # Place formula in the center of visual area (spanning B3 to D6)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B3", "D6", scale_factor=1.3)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.
        # Highlight P(A) in #FFFF00 and label it 'Prior'.
        prior_label = Text("Prior", font_size=24, color=PRIOR_COLOR)
        # P(A) is part 4 in the numerator
        self.place_at_grid(prior_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(DIM_COLOR),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PRIOR_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(
            formula[4].animate.set_color(PRIOR_COLOR),
            FadeIn(prior_label, shift=UP*0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.
        # Highlight P(B|A) in #00FF00 and label it 'Likelihood'.
        likelihood_label = Text("Likelihood", font_size=24, color=LIKELIHOOD_COLOR)
        # P(B|A) is part 3 in the numerator
        self.place_at_grid(likelihood_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(DIM_COLOR),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(LIKELIHOOD_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(
            formula[3].animate.set_color(LIKELIHOOD_COLOR),
            FadeIn(likelihood_label, shift=UP*0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Divide by the total probability of that evidence.
        # Highlight P(B) in #00FFFF and label it 'Evidence'.
        evidence_label = Text("Evidence", font_size=24, color=EVIDENCE_COLOR)
        # P(B) is part 6 in the denominator
        self.place_at_grid(evidence_label, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(DIM_COLOR),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(EVIDENCE_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(
            formula[6].animate.set_color(EVIDENCE_COLOR),
            FadeIn(evidence_label, shift=DOWN*0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Now you have the updated posterior probability.
        # Highlight P(A|B) in #FF00FF and label it 'Posterior'.
        posterior_label = Text("Posterior", font_size=24, color=POSTERIOR_COLOR)
        # P(A|B) is part 0 on the left side
        self.place_at_grid(posterior_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(DIM_COLOR),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(POSTERIOR_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        color_posterior = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors
        formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        # index 2 is P(B|A)
        formula[2].set_color(color_likelihood)
        # index 4 is P(A)
        formula[4].set_color(color_prior)
        # index 6 is P(B)
        formula[6].set_color(color_evidence)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Replace P(B|A) with P(B)
        # New likelihood term
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Sliding animation: show the swap
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.shift(UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(new_likelihood, shift=DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Strike through P(B) in numerator and denominator
        strike_num = Line(
            new_likelihood.get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            new_likelihood.get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        strike_den = Line(
            formula[6].get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            formula[6].get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(strike_num), Create(strike_den))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final result: P(A|B) = P(A)
        final_formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)",
            font_size=42
        )
        final_formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        final_formula[2].set_color(color_prior)
        self.place_in_area(final_formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(VGroup(new_likelihood, strike_num, formula[6], strike_den, formula[3], formula[5])),
            Transform(formula[0], final_formula[0]),
            Transform(formula[1], final_formula[1]),
            Transform(formula[4], final_formula[2])
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and the Logic of Independence
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with basic probability knowledge.

sections.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating belief' through a story. A detective dog named 'Sherlock Bones' hears a rustle in the bushes. He thinks there's a 10% chance it's a cat. If it were a cat, his ears would twitch with 90% certainty. His ears just twitched. Does this mean it's definitely a cat? This sets the stage for prior vs. posterior probability.
sections.example: Visual: Sherlock Bones with a thought bubble showing a 'Cat' (10%) and 'Wind' (90%). An animation shows his ears twitching as the 'new evidence'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Conditional Probability & The Shrinking Universe
sections.content: Explain P(A|B) using a Venn Diagram. Emphasize that 'Given B' means our 'Universe' (Sample Space) shrinks from the whole rectangle to just circle B. We are now looking for the area where A and B overlap within that new, smaller circle.
sections.example: Animation: A large square (Total Probability) fades out, leaving only a glowing circle 'B'. A small slice of 'A' inside 'B' is highlighted to represent P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).

sections.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
sections.content: Define Independence. If A and B are independent, knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). This means the 'proportion' of A inside B is the same as A's proportion in the whole universe.
sections.example: Visual: Two circles (A and B) that don't overlap in a way that suggests dependency. If we zoom into B, the percentage of A remains exactly the same as it was in the original square.

sections.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
sections.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).
sections.example: Graphic: A balance scale. On one side is our 'Prior belief' (P(A)). We add 'Evidence' (the Likelihood ratio) to tip the scale toward the 'Posterior' result.

sections.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
sections.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.
sections.example: Tree Diagram: Start with 1,000 chips. Branch into 10 Defective and 990 Healthy. Show the robot's 'Beep' paths. Most beeps actually come from healthy chips (False Positives), surprising the learner.

sections.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
sections.content: Briefly explain what happens to Bayes' Theorem if events are independent. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) simply equals P(A). The evidence B becomes 'noise' and doesn't update our belief about A at all.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Bayes Machine' where the input 'Evidence B' passes through a filter. If B is independent of A, the output (Posterior) is identical to the input (Prior).

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
sections.content: Summarize: 1. Bayes' Theorem is a way to update beliefs. 2. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 3. Always consider the Prior (the base rate) before jumping to conclusions.
sections.example: Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat' after combining his twitching ears with the base rate of cats in the neighborhood.
